Hi Jose — thanks for the clear list. We can absolutely deliver a consolidated implementation plan and the attribute/role matrices.

Quick notes up front:
- SCIM: Redwood supports SCIM 2.0; we offer both bulk (one-time) imports and incremental delta syncs using /Users and /Groups endpoints. Delta syncs use If-None-Match/ETag checks and sequence tokens for high-throughput directories.
- Auth: SCIM API supports API keys scoped to the tenant; we recommend rotating keys every 90 days. For providers requiring short-lived credentials we support OAuth2 client credentials for the SCIM connector.
- SSO: We support SAML 2.0 (IdP-initiated and SP-initiated) and OIDC. We provide a sample SAML metadata file and a JSON OIDC client config.

I'll assemble a single PDF with details, sample manifests (attribute mappings), and an admin-controls matrix. Target: delivery by Thu EOD (2026-08-12). If you need it sooner, let me know — we can prioritize.

Sharing this thread internally to Ben and Marissa to pick up technical details and audit retention numbers.

Thanks,
Evelyn Hart

Evelyn — notes below (kept short per request):

1) Bulk import: CSV and JSON import supported. CSV template (attached) requires columns: externalId, userName, displayName, givenName, familyName, emails[type=work,value], groups (comma-separated). We include an optional "sourceId" column to track origin. For one-time migrations we recommend POST /scim/v2/Users in batches of 500.

2) Delta sync: We support long-polling and ETag-based delta on /Users endpoint. For very large directories we provide a sequence token model (cursor) so clients can request changes since last token; typical delta latency <60s for normal load. Collision handling: if two users share the same email we create a conflict flag and do NOT merge automatically. Admins must resolve via the UI or SCIM PATCH to correct externalId mapping. Default behavior is to reject ambiguous create requests and return 409 with a conflict payload.

3) Auth model: SCIM keys are tenant-scoped API keys (rotate via Console or API). Support for OAuth2 client credentials for third-party connectors if customers prefer short-lived creds.

Attached: scim-bulk-template.csv (stub).

Ben
Senior Solutions Engineer

From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.ai>

Jose — attaching the consolidated implementation plan and matrices as requested. Highlights and clarifications are below. If you want, we can schedule a 30-minute call to walk through the mapping and the migration steps.

Highlights (summary):
- SCIM: RFC 7644-compatible endpoints (POST /Users, GET /Users, PATCH /Users, GET /Users/{id}); bulk imports supported with batch sizes up to 500; delta syncs via sequence tokens and ETag; conflict resolution returns explicit 409 responses and flags for admin review.
- Attribute mapping: default mapped attributes are: externalId -> externalId, userName -> email, name.givenName/familyName, emails[type=work] -> primaryEmail, groups -> groupMembership. We provide a sample CSV and a JSON attribute map for edge cases (attached).
- RBAC: exposed roles (customer-facing): Organization Owner (full), Org Admin (manage users, groups, settings), User Manager (provision/deprovision users), Read-only Auditor (view-only, export logs). See attached admin-controls-matrix.xlsx for exact allowed API and Console actions per role.
- Audit & retention: Provisioning and SSO events are logged to our audit pipeline (immutable event store) and mirrored to customer-owned S3 buckets on request. Default retention in the platform: 365 days for provisioning events; optional extended retention available as an add-on (up to 7 years). Logs include timestamp, actor (internal/external API key), action, target resource, delta payload.
- SSO: We support SAML 2.0 and OIDC. SAML attributes: NameID (email), eduPersonPrincipalName optional, plus custom attribute mapping. OIDC claim mapping supported via a JSON mapping file. We include example SAML metadata and OIDC client config in the attachments.

Attachments (zipped appendix): redwood-scim-implementation-plan.pdf (detailed step-by-step), saml-oidc-mapping.csv (example attribute/claim mappings), admin-controls-matrix.xlsx (role capability matrix), scim-bulk-template.csv.

If you need an export in a different format or a redline for their procurement team, say the word. Happy to join the call with your team to walk through migration timelines (we typically see 2–4 weeks for directories <10k users).

Regards,
Evelyn Hart
Head of Customer Security & Compliance
Redwood Inference
